results.name: Dangerous Linux capabilities present
results.description: Inspects CapEff in /proc/self/status and flags any capability commonly used as a stepping stone to container escape.
evidence: CAP_SYS_ADMIN (near-root inside the container; many escapes pivot through it)
results.recommendation: Drop capabilities you don't need (--cap-drop=ALL then --cap-add only the strictly required) or set securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"] in Kubernetes.

results.name: Container runtime socket exposed
results.description: Detects whether docker.sock, containerd.sock or crio.sock are reachable from inside the container — equivalent to giving root on the host.
evidence: runtime socket(s) reachable from inside the container:
results.recommendation: Never bind-mount the runtime socket into a workload. If the container needs to talk to the cluster API, use a ServiceAccount with a least-privilege RBAC role instead.
